requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

findings.claim: An unrelated wire-format change rides along with this bug fix. Removing the `case <= byte.MaxValue: TryWriteUInt8` branch means values 128..255 are no longer written as uint8 (0xcc, 2 bytes). They fall through to uint16 (0xcd, 3 bytes). Serialized output changes for every such value: it is larger, no longer the minimal MessagePack encoding, and byte-incompatible with base. REQ-2283 is a generator/analyzer crash fix and asks for no runtime serialization change, so this contradicts 'nothing beyond the requirement' and is a breaking change.

receipt_plan.detail: Build base and head. For values 127, 128, 200 and 255, call the MessagePackPrimitives.TryWrite overload containing this switch (and MessagePackSerializer.Serialize on the matching unsigned type). Compare bytes: base gives [0xcc, 0xc8] for 200, head is expected to give [0xcd, 0x00, 0xc8].

findings.claim: An unrelated change in the uint writer removes the `case <= byte.MaxValue` → `TryWriteUInt8` branch. Values 128..255 are now written as uint16 (0xcd, 3 bytes) instead of uint8 (0xcc, 2 bytes). The output is still decodable, but it is no longer the most compact encoding. It changes the serialized bytes for every such value written through this path, which is a wire-format change outside the scope of REQ-2283.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ReceiptsUInt8RangeEncodingTests.UInt32_InUInt8Range_UsesUInt8Encoding (values 128, 200, 255). It expects written == 2 and buffer[0] == 0xcc, and it fails on head with written == 3 and buffer[0] == 0xcd. A byte-diff of MessagePackSerializer.Serialize(200u) between base and head would also show the difference.

findings.claim: The case for values in 128..255 was removed from the uint-writing switch in MessagePackPrimitives, so those values now go to TryWriteUInt16 and are encoded as 0xcd + 2 bytes instead of the canonical 0xcc + 1 byte. This changes the serialized bytes for every user of that method and is unrelated to the generator crash. Payloads grow by 1 byte, and byte-exact comparisons, hashes and signatures change.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize values 127, 128, 200 and 255 (as uint, or as the integer type that reaches this method) using base-built and head-built MessagePack. Compare the bytes: base gives CC 80, CC C8 and CC FF, while head gives CD 00 80, CD 00 C8 and CD 00 FF.

findings.claim: The switch in the unsigned-integer writer drops the `<= byte.MaxValue` case, so values 128..255 now fall through to TryWriteUInt16 and are encoded as uint16 (0xcd) instead of the canonical uint8 (0xcc). Output is non-canonical and larger. Readers still decode it, so this is not a security hole. The change is unrelated to the requirement and alters the wire format, so it breaks byte-compat for hash- or signature-based consumers, and any strict-format expectations.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize uint values 128, 200 and 255 (and an int in that range) with base-built and head-built MessagePack. Compare bytes: base emits CC xx, head emits CD 00 xx. Also run the existing MessagePackWriter/Primitives tests.

findings.claim: Unrelated change to the serializer runtime: the `case <= byte.MaxValue` branch (TryWriteUInt8) is removed from the unsigned-integer writer. Values 128..255 would now be written as UInt16 (0xcd) instead of UInt8 (0xcc). This changes the wire format, wastes bytes, and is out of scope for a generator/analyzer crash fix; it is also likely to break byte-exact tests.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize uint/ulong values such as 128, 200 and 255 with base-built and head-built MessagePack and compare bytes. Base emits 0xcc 0xNN; head emits 0xcd 0x00 0xNN. Also run the MessagePackWriter/primitives unit tests.

findings.claim: The change deletes the `case <= byte.MaxValue` branch in the unsigned-integer writer (UInt8 encoding for values 128..255). This is unrelated to REQ-2283. Values 128..255 now fall to the UInt16 branch and encode as 0xCD 2 bytes instead of 0xCC 1 byte, which changes the wire format and is not minimal. No test in the diff covers it.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize uint/ulong/int values 128..255 (e.g. 200) with base-built and head-built MessagePack and compare bytes: expect base 0xCC 0xC8 vs head 0xCD 0x00 0xC8. Also run the existing MessagePackWriter/primitives tests.

findings.claim: The fix to GetPropertyIdentifierLocation (BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull) is never exercised. No test makes a metadata property have a null key. Reverting it to DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] would not fail any new test. Likewise the MemberNeedsKey FirstOrDefault change is only exercised by the UnkeyedMember test, whose type is reached via a path that may exit earlier.

hunches.claim: The wrapper only filters diagnostics after Diagnostic.Create has already run, so it cannot prevent a crash. Any remaining direct `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` index in GetObjectInfo still throws for the metadata closed-generic struct. The reporter named three sites (735, 1009, 1101). The diff only changes the two at new lines 985 and 1077. No hunk touches the first site, which would be about 27 lines earlier, near line 708 under the same offset. If that site is reached for `Item<int>` from a referenced assembly, CS8785/AD0001 still occur and acceptance criteria 1-4 are unmet.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile lib (`[MessagePackObject] public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);` plus `struct Item2<T>` with a [Key(0)] field) to a MetadataReference via EmitToImageReference. Compile app with `Cmd` holding `[Key(1)] public Item<int> Member` and a `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class R {}`. Run CSharpGeneratorDriver with MessagePackGenerator and assert GetRunResult().Results[0].Exception is null and a resolver file is generated. Also run compilation.WithAnalyzers(MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer) and assert there is no AD0001. Separately, grep TypeCollector.cs for `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`.

hunches.claim: The wrapper in TypeCollector drops every diagnostic whose location is not in the compilation's syntax trees. This includes diagnostics with Location.None, which is what AOTDerivedKeyAttribute or other diagnostics produce when the location is null. Previously these were reported, so users may lose existing MsgPack004/MemberNeedsKey and similar diagnostics. For example, MemberNeedsKey on a source type whose location resolves to null is now suppressed. The filter also applies to all diagnostics, not just those from metadata symbols.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer tests (MsgPack003/004/005/etc.) on source types, plus a case with a diagnostic using a null or None location. Verify that the expected diagnostics still appear. Also check for diagnostics reported on partial or generated trees outside the compilation.

hunches.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose location is not in the compilation. It also drops diagnostics with a null Location, which Diagnostic.Create turns into Location.None. Diagnostics that guard users against insecure or unsupported configurations can then be silently lost whenever a location lookup returns null, for example GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returning null for a non-PropertyDeclarationSyntax such as a record positional parameter. The result is a silent failure to warn, not a crash. The diagnostics affected are mostly compile-time diagnostics such as MsgPack004 and MsgPack00x, so the security impact is low.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an analyzer test with a [MessagePackObject] record whose positional property lacks a Key and has a null location. Assert that the expected MsgPack diagnostic is still reported, before and after the change.

hunches.claim: The ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the current compilation, for all diagnostics routed through reportDiagnostic. This includes diagnostics created with a null location (e.g. MemberNeedsKey from FirstOrDefault()), and any diagnostic for source-less cases in the current compilation, which will now be silently suppressed. It is a broad behaviour change beyond the three crash sites. It is consistent with [L12] for metadata types, but could hide legitimate diagnostics, such as ones with Location.None for in-compilation symbols.

receipt_plan.detail: Add analyzer tests for diagnostics that previously reported with Location.None or additional locations (e.g. MsgPack004 on a property without a declaring syntax reference in the same compilation) and confirm they are still reported. Run the full analyzer test suite for regressions.

hunches.claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper filters every diagnostic whose location is not in the compilation, including the null-location diagnostics produced by FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax(). No test asserts that diagnostics for source-declared types are still reported (the MsgPack004 MemberNeedsKey and BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull cases). If the guard were removed, or the IsInSource condition negated, the new tests (which expect zero diagnostics) would still pass for the metadata case. Mutants on the guard are only weakly detected; existing analyzer tests are not in this diff.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1446 negate-condition: if (diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && ...) -> if (!(diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && ...)); expected to survive in the new tests because they only assert no diagnostics for metadata types and add no positive in-source diagnostic case. Run only the three new tests.

hunches.claim: The reporter named three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (issue lines 735, 1009, 1101). The diff guards only the two near old lines 985 and 1077. No hunk touches the first site. The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper cannot protect it, because the location argument is evaluated when Diagnostic.Create runs, before the wrapper is invoked. If that path is reachable for a metadata type, the IndexOutOfRangeException in the generator and analyzer remains, and the acceptance criterion 'diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the symbol has no declaring syntax' is only partly met.

receipt_plan.detail: grep head TypeCollector.cs for `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. Any remaining hit reachable from GetObjectInfo is unguarded. Confirm by running Req2283ClosedGenericStructFromReferencedAssemblyTests, extended with a lib type that triggers that diagnostic.

hunches.claim: BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull is now silently dropped for record positional properties declared in the compiling assembly, e.g. `record R([property: Key((string)null)] string X)`. For such a property, DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] is a ParameterSyntax, not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax. GetPropertyIdentifierLocation therefore returns null, the diagnostic gets Location.None, and the new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper discards it because the location is not in source. The base code crashed here on the cast; head reports nothing for a source symbol that should get the error. A fallback to item.Locations[0], or handling ParameterSyntax, is needed.

receipt_plan.detail: Read GetPropertyIdentifierLocation (TypeCollector.cs:1434), which uses `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax` and returns null for a ParameterSyntax. Then read ReportIfLocatedInCompilation (TypeCollector.cs:1444), which requires Location.IsInSource. To confirm, run the analyzer on a C# 9 positional record with `[property: Key((string)null)]` and observe that no BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic is reported.

hunches.claim: The new tests bypass the real two-project flow. The first and third tests use LanguageVersion.CSharp7_3, and the first and third have a class-based consumer. The analyzer-side test uses SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck, so the generated output is never checked and only a hint name is asserted. The tests never check that a formatter for the closed generic is registered, as the requirement says trimmed and AOT apps need. Whether the resolver is complete is unasserted.

receipt_plan.detail: RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync sets TestBehaviors.SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck and asserts only Assert.Contains(hintName); no check that the resolver content is correct or includes the closed-generic formatter.
